- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) is a standardized method for rating the severity of security vulnerabilities in software.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The CVSS score is usually provided for each Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] CVE is a database that contains identifiers for publicly known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When a new CVE is published, it often includes an associated CVSS score to help organizations understand the severity of the vulnerability and prioritize remediation efforts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There might be cases where a CVE does not have an immediate CVSS score upon release, and the score may be added later as the vulnerability is analyzed further.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] CVEs along with their CVSS scores can be found on websites like the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) and MITRE's CVE database.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The National Vulnerability Database (NVD) can be accessed at <https://nvd.nist.gov/>.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] MITRE's CVE database can be accessed at <https://cve.mitre.org/>.
